subject: Sprint Slate + MAP proposal — week-by-week acceptance and kickoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cloudlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint Slate + MAP proposal — week-by-week acceptance and kickoff

Alex — great to meet last week. Follow-up with the initial Sprint Slate (MAP) we discussed. I sketched a compact 6-week evaluation that prioritizes a small integration, performance validation, and an acceptance gate that maps directly to your procurement milestones. Attached: a Google Doc template with roles/owners and an acceptance matrix, plus a starter slide deck for a 30-minute kickoff.

Key asks / proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 0 (kickoff): align stakeholders, enable test account, share baseline prompt set.
- Week 1–2: integration + smoke tests (tech owner: Karthik) — target 95% success on inference calls under expected load.
- Week 3–4: qualitative eval + edge-case prompts; establish quality thresholds and sample prompts.
- Week 5: cost/latency review, final performance tuning.
- Week 6: acceptance gate + procurement sign-off.

Open items I left as placeholders in the doc: explicit success metrics for your SLA window, and the procurement timing. If this outline looks reasonable I can turn the placeholders into concrete checkpoints (test definitions, sample payloads, sign-off owners) and share an updated GDoc.

Attachments/links:
- MAP_SprintSlate_v1.gdoc (outline + acceptance matrix) — https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2B3C-MAP-SprintSlate-v1
- Kickoff_Slides_SprintSlate_v1.gslides — https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1X9Y8Z-Kickoff-Slides

Next step: can we lock a 30-minute kickoff for next Tuesday or Wednesday? I included Marissa and Karthik to handle success criteria and technical validation.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.com]

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cloudlytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Erin Mills <erin@cloudlytics.com>, Procurement <procurement@cloudlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint Slate + MAP proposal — week-by-week acceptance and kickoff

Jordan — thanks, this looks promising and much tighter than our usual kickoff docs. A few clarifying Qs before we lock dates: 

1) Success metric detail: what exactly will you accept as the ‘95% success on inference calls’? Is that 95% non-error responses, or 95% within latency X ms? We need both reliability and p95 latency defined to sign off.
2) Data handling: for our POC will logs/token data be retained by Redwood? If so, what's the default retention and can we opt for shorter retention for this pilot?
3) Procurement timing: our internal procurement window opens the week of July 6; if acceptance is the end of Week 6 (as proposed), that aligns, but we may need a formal evaluation summary and an invoice-ready statement of work.

Also looping Erin (legal/procurement partner) and Procurement mailbox — Erin, can you confirm any doc or evidence you need in the acceptance packet?

Happy to take the kickoff next Tue at 10am PT if that works for your team — tentative until we confirm attendees.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Director of Platform Engineering
CloudLytics
alex.rivera@cloudlytics.com

On Tue, Jun 16, 2026 at 09:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — great to meet last week. Follow-up with the initial Sprint Slate (MAP) we discussed...

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Sprint Slate + MAP proposal — week-by-week acceptance and kickoff

Thanks Alex — good questions. Short answers inline and I also updated the GDoc (link below) with concrete checkpoints.

1) Success metrics: we’ll use two gates — reliability (>=98% success = non-500 responses and no model-side errors) and p95 latency <= 500ms for the baseline payloads we list in the doc. Those are keyed in the Acceptance Matrix under Week 2 and Week 5 rows. I left room to tighten p95 if your infra requires lower latency.
2) Data handling: for the pilot we run logs and telemetry for troubleshooting; default retention is 30 days but we can set a customer-specific retention to 7 days for this POC. That’s an option in the private config I noted in the doc (see Data Handling section).
3) Procurement packet: we’ll produce a short evaluation summary (1 page) plus an artifacts bundle (sample logs, test run screenshots, and the acceptance matrix). We can also provide the SOC-2 evidence bundle link if Erin needs it.

I updated the GDoc with the full acceptance matrix and added an initial sample payloads sheet. Please review: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2B3C-MAP-SprintSlate-v1 (v1.1 — acceptance criteria added).

If Tue 10am PT works, I’ll send the invite and include a 10–15 minute tech deep-dive for Karthik to confirm integration points.

—Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
